Hout Bay: A harbour in decline

By: Liz Fish | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Hout Bay harbour is on the top of the list for any tourist visiting Cape Town but its literally being taken apart by cable thieves and demolition crews and DPW stands

Unique Selling Point:
Once a thriving harbour, still one of the top destinations for tourists visiting Cape Town is in decline, it's under siege by petty criminals. A major factory once employing over 100 people has been taken apart brick by brink in broad day light and the harbour master and DPW have done nothing to halt the removal of a valuable asset. It's a harbour in decline with derelict boats clogging up the quayside. Petty criminals have stripped cables, steal millions of rands worth of metal off the boats, and even sink them by stripping their brass stop cocks.

Summary:
Oceana rented a factory in Hout Bay from DPW for many years, the fish meal plant provided work for 100's of people in the Hangberg community but was forced to close down it's operations because of complaints about the smell. In December 2021 the lease came to an end and they handed it back to DPW. Within weeks the roof was stripped, then a few months later people from outside Hout Bay moved in and began to removing any metal inside the factory. Gregg Louw's cousin lost his life falling from the rafters but the looting continued. How did DPW stand by and watch as millions of rands worth of infra structure and building that had plenty of tenets willing to move in and pay rent, creating infrastructure and provide employment, do nothing?

Further information:
Snoekies the oldest tenet in Hout Bay harbour dates back to the 50's- the owner Justine Strong took over the running of the business 12 years ago and has invested R13 million in the operation, employing 80 local residents. He is operating on a month to month lease- despite having been promised on two occasions that he is entitled to a long term lease. Most tenets in the harbour have been on month to month leases for years. Its difficult to invest without long term tenure yet they do, providing security for their operations. Justin knowing the Oceana lease was coming to an end applied to take over some of the factory as did 20 potential tenants. Many people are willing to invest in Hout Bay harbour despite the obvious security challenges but the DPW doesn't have a clear mandate. They allowed the building to stand empty despite tenets raising the alarm. Hangberg residents are as concerned and have seen how previous factories like the Sea Harvest can be turned into thriving tourist attractions like the Hout Bay Market and provide employment.

Gregg Louw runs a charter boat service and is a Hangberg resident and the vice chair of the Hangberg Peace and Mediation forum. His cousin fell to his death in the Oceana factory while stripping it for steel. As a respected member of the community his plea to DPW fell on deaf ears- he alerted them to the stripping of the roof last December - no security was put in place. Now 3 months later after copper thieves set the Bluefin factory alight when they tried to steal a cable DPW have deployed 15 armed guards. He asks why when criminals are caught and arrested are they set free- its sending out the wrong message.

Roger Bigaigon- has been in the harbour since he was 17, son of a Portuguese fishermen. The Portuguese are an important part of the fishing community. Roger built factories and ran dellies in Hout Bay harbour, and has 3 boats moored there currently, guarded by local residents who sleep on his boats to protect them. He says there is no security, the harbour infrastructure like the slip way is in disrepair but he is prepared to pay to get it fixed. The fishing industry has been destroyed by DEFF by removing quotas and issuing paper quotas, boat owners can't afford to run their boats, never mind repair them. Roger says a public private partnership is possible if DPW and DEFF would just act on their small harbour development policy.

Press Release:


The iconic Hout Bay harbour – top of the itinerary for many visitors to Cape Town, if only for the best serving of snoek and chips in the country – is being torn apart by copper thieves, tik addicts, vandals, and opportunistic criminals. Why is the Department of Public Works and the Harbour Master doing almost nothing to change the fortunes of the once-thriving harbour? What could have been a hub of economic progress for the communities that depend on the infrastructure of the harbour is fast becoming a no man’s land, stripped bare of anything that could earn pilferers quick cash.

Script:


Upsound with drone shot
Script: This was once a thriving fishing community, bustling with boats bringing in their catches
LINK Hout Bay harbour top of the list for anybody visiting Cape Town and little wonder, the most stunning bay and a romantic beach to take a gentle stroll with your partner or your dog

And what is reputed to be the best fish and chips in the country

Script: Today it’s a harbour on life support - clogged with derelict boats and plagued by crime.
Upsound Roger “It gets enough people coming here like the V & A, so they should invest.”
Script: Roger Biagonon has worked here all his life, starting on his father’s boat when he was 17.
Roger: 30 years ago it was a major hub. I mean, boats were working in and out, it was movement of tourist fishermen, there was a lot more security, there was a lot of life.
Derek: What's changed?

Roger: Fishing is depleted. The tuna is not biting. You can’t afford to go to sea. So the crew don't earn, and then also the closing down of companies that have taken many jobs to the local community. And the buildings and the harbor, and everything is just deteriorating 00:01:32:29 it's causing problems for us fishermen, the community and the harbour. It's it's it's it's very sad.

Script: In the 50’s, the fishermen would buy soup and bait from an old bus at the harbour called Snoekies. Now a restaurant, it was bought 12 years ago by Justin Strong.

Upsound” Clip 83 00.15 “ We have got a signed lease agreement here from the 15th November 1957 and that that building right there, it still stands

Script: But for the last few months the harbour has been under siege by criminals
Driving Justin .so it’s a great mixed use harbour and a massive amount of potential…. And then this is the most disheartening thing I've probably seen in my entire life, these are the late Oceana buildings, there is nothing left. ……….it looks like Mariupol literally looks like a bomb has gone off.
LINK “Just how do you take apart an entire factory over 13000 square meters in broad day light I am talking about the entire roof, electric cables and pipes, even the very bricks walked out of here, and authorities turned a blind eye”
GREG: We were worried because you've got a lot of traffic, people walking past the factory 

Script: Gregg Louw is a community leader from the nearby Hangberg village. Once, he says, a boy nearly died stealing electric cables from the warehouse. After that, the dismantling started in earnest and when the wind threatened to tear off the roofing, he alerted the authorities. 

Derek: So who did you contact?

Gregg: I contacted the Public Works, the harbourmaster and as well as actually the person responsible for properties.

Derek: What was his response

Gregg: look, if roof sheets must come down, and hits somebody it's an act of nature.

Script: Greg was horrified. Tragically, just a few days later, his own cousin fell to his death from the roof.

Gregg  They on drugs on tik and everything  ……all they could see here .there is money to be made actually on on the material, he was on that roof itself and unfortunately something happened and he came down
 
Script: The factory is central to this community’s history: providing jobs for more than 50 years, it employed over 200 people in its heyday. In recent times, though, it was forced to cut production and in December 2019, closed its doors for good. Ownership fell to the Department of Public Works but there was no shortage of interest in leasing the site.

Justin: 00:00:44:09 Since 2019, we've been trying to negotiate 3800 square meters here, possible 60 to 100 jobs over the next 3 to 5 years and nothing happened

Script: And Justin has good reason to be interested in the site. Just meters away from the rubble is a shining example of what’s possible in a public/private partnership and a bit of creative thinking.

LINK It’s clear there is fantastic potential like right here. The Bay Harbour market, this used to be a fish factory now a thriving business, a good example of what is possible

Script: It’s a thriving venue, staffed by locals and often packed on weekends with people blissfully unaware of the trouble festering in the harbour across the road.

Derek: But Surely that is security for them as well.

Justin: Absolutely. Job creation, empowerment, investment in their building because we lease the properties.

Script: But there’s a catch.

Justin “So we've spent just in the last 12 months, a million rand improving these buildings with cold storage and power supply. Well, so and we have no lease month to month lease, so we just acting in good faith. 

Script: For the last 3 years virtually every tenant is operating on the same short term lease, creating uncertainty and increasing financial risk.
Gregg: A decade ago government spent 10 million to come up with a plan of how these harbours would function now and contribute towards our economy.
Script: In 2018 Stakeholders and tenets were shown an elaborate plan of how the harbour would be redeveloped and 20 year leases discussed
Justin We've been promised a long term lease verbally in a meeting with high level government officials in Hermanus some 7 to 8 years ago, it was said in front of everyone, what would Hout bay be without Snoekies ? You will get leases
Script: But since then nothing has happened. Tenets can’t get an explanation from the Department of Public works as to why they are all on month to month leases, but Gregg has a suggestion

Gregg The state also faced the issue around transformation specific on this harbour, because most of the tenants on these harbours are still white .
Derek: To put it crudely, Greg, they didn't want white investors with long term leases
Gregg: I would say yes

Script: Government’s lack of communication isn’t helping an already fraught situation. Short term leases and an apparent criminal free-for-all has led to mounting discontent - much of it directed at the harbour master, Phumla Feni Gela. She’s a government appointee tasked with running the harbour but, after her office was torched by alleged poachers, critics say she’s seldom seen.

BREATH 

Script: Meanwhile, the Oceana factory fully destroyed, the thieves worked their way through the harbour, removing cables and drain covers; the tenants arriving each morning to less and less infrastructure. 

Upsound “Stolen cut here at 1 o'clock in the morning right in front if the security office
Script: After another abandoned factory was torched at the harbour last month, the Department of Public works finally reacted, deploying armed guards. Crime dropped 60% as a result but, like the tenets, they’re on a month to month contract. 
LINK This may come as no surprise but this is a complex setup between two different government departments, so public works owns the land and some of the buildings, but fisheries operates the harbour so there is massive confusion as who is responsible for what along of cause with passing of the proverbial buck
Justin: I speak to DPW please can I get security? They say it's not our Department, it's the harbourmaster department . I go back to the harbourmaster. Madam Harbormaster, please, can we get security? No, no, no. I'm only access, control and anything to do with the boats, the wharf, the piers. Amongst ourselves there was probably about eight of us and we were spending about R400 000 a month on security, which we shouldn't be spending.

Script: Another frustration and key to the Harbour Master’s job is running the dry dock - or slip- where wooden boats are maintained annually. At least, that’s the theory…

Roger: there was some cable theft about two weeks ago or three weeks ago. ….…..this is one of our crucial part of our business. We have to come up once a year. You need to do surveys for Samsa and obviously repaint and check the boats and make sure that it's seaworthy for our safety of our crews.

Derek: Looks like everything's slipping around here .

Roger: This is supposed to be the repair key. …But now this one sunken we don't know how we're going to function this year because that one is completely blocking the small slipway

Script: Manna Newman has been fixing the wooden boats in this harbour for 30 years, and his livelihood depends on a functioning slip.

Derek: So are you saying the harbourmaster isn't doing her job?

Manna: She's not doing the job. The way I see it should be done, if you got input from people that knows the industry for long years, then you take that advice and understand and you also communicate with the community , because if you don't communicate with the community and you just do your own thing, you're going to get problems at the end of the day.

Script: In her absence, Manna claims the harbour master’s responsibilities have fallen to a junior official.

LINK This is the harbour master office, our request for an interview have gone nowhere for the past few weeks, so we are here to get her side of the story
Upsound- can we come and talk to the harbour master, she is not here at the current moment
LINK Well apparently it’s not that uncommon that the harbour master is not in her office,
Script: Her critics claim she is distracted by a couple of side hustles
Script: We decided to give her a call
ON Camera Good afternoon is that the harbour master- we have been trying to get an interview with you
Phumla “No you must speak to my seniors they are aware of what is going on
Derek” There are complaints that you are seldom in the harbour, that you are, that you are more concerned with doing your own business selling health and beauty products and running your church
Phumla”No they must speak to my seniors they are aware of that
Derek” But you are in charge of the harbour, …..there are huge complaints there are poachers that take off in front of your office in broad daylight
Phumla “ no if have a complaint and you want it to be sorted you must speak to my seniors in Cape
Town in head office
Script: After weeks of trying, the Department of Public Works was unable to arrange an interview with Minister, Patricia De Lille. And in the absence of answers, the poachers continue coming and going, boat owners pay for repairs to the slip and lift sunken vessels, and the tenants defend themselves against a tide of criminality by paying for their own security.

LINK This is the harbour master office, our request for an interview have gone nowhere for the past few weeks, so we are here to get her side of the story Upsound- can we come and talk to the harbour master, she is not here at the current moment LINK Well apparently it’s not that uncommon that the harbour master is not in her office, Script: Her critics claim she is distracted by a couple of side hustles Script: We decided to give her a call ON Camera Good afternoon is that the harbour master- we have been trying to get an interview with you Phumla “No you must speak to my seniors they are aware of what is going on Derek” There are complaints that you are seldom in the harbour, that you are, that you are more concerned with doing your own business selling health and beauty products and running your church Phumla”No they must speak to my seniors they are aware of that Derek” But you are in charge of the harbour, …..there are huge complaints there are poachers that take off in front of your office in broad daylight Phumla “ no if have a complaint and you want it to be sorted you must speak to my seniors in Cape Town in head office Script: After weeks of trying, the Department of Public Works was unable to arrange an interview with Minister, Patricia De Lille. And in the absence of answers, the poachers continue coming and going, boat owners pay for repairs to the slip and lift sunken vessels, and the tenants defend themselves against a tide of criminality by paying for their own security. metadata.Unique Selling Point: Once a thriving harbour, still one of the top destinations for tourists visiting Cape Town is in decline, it's under siege by petty criminals. A major factory once employing over 100 people has been taken apart brick by brink in broad day light and the harbour master and DPW have done nothing to halt the removal of a valuable asset. It's a harbour in decline with derelict boats clogging up the quayside. Petty criminals have stripped cables, steal millions of rands worth of metal off the boats, and even sink them by stripping their brass stop cocks.
metadata.Summary: Oceana rented a factory in Hout Bay from DPW for many years, the fish meal plant provided work for 100's of people in the Hangberg community but was forced to close down it's operations because of complaints about the smell. In December 2021 the lease came to an end and they handed it back to DPW. Within weeks the roof was stripped, then a few months later people from outside Hout Bay moved in and began to removing any metal inside the factory. Gregg Louw's cousin lost his life falling from the rafters but the looting continued. How did DPW stand by and watch as millions of rands worth of infra structure and building that had plenty of tenets willing to move in and pay rent, creating infrastructure and provide employment, do nothing?
metadata.Further information: Snoekies the oldest tenet in Hout Bay harbour dates back to the 50's- the owner Justine Strong took over the running of the business 12 years ago and has invested R13 million in the operation, employing 80 local residents. He is operating on a month to month lease- despite having been promised on two occasions that he is entitled to a long term lease. Most tenets in the harbour have been on month to month leases for years. Its difficult to invest without long term tenure yet they do, providing security for their operations. Justin knowing the Oceana lease was coming to an end applied to take over some of the factory as did 20 potential tenants. Many people are willing to invest in Hout Bay harbour despite the obvious security challenges but the DPW doesn't have a clear mandate. They allowed the building to stand empty despite tenets raising the alarm. Hangberg residents are as concerned and have seen how previous factories like the Sea Harvest can be turned into thriving tourist attractions like the Hout Bay Market and provide employment. Gregg Louw runs a charter boat service and is a Hangberg resident and the vice chair of the Hangberg Peace and Mediation forum. His cousin fell to his death in the Oceana factory while stripping it for steel. As a respected member of the community his plea to DPW fell on deaf ears- he alerted them to the stripping of the roof last December - no security was put in place. Now 3 months later after copper thieves set the Bluefin factory alight when they tried to steal a cable DPW have deployed 15 armed guards. He asks why when criminals are caught and arrested are they set free- its sending out the wrong message. Roger Bigaigon- has been in the harbour since he was 17, son of a Portuguese fishermen. The Portuguese are an important part of the fishing community. Roger built factories and ran dellies in Hout Bay harbour, and has 3 boats moored there currently, guarded by local residents who sleep on his boats to protect them. He says there is no security, the harbour infrastructure like the slip way is in disrepair but he is prepared to pay to get it fixed. The fishing industry has been destroyed by DEFF by removing quotas and issuing paper quotas, boat owners can't afford to run their boats, never mind repair them. Roger says a public private partnership is possible if DPW and DEFF would just act on their small harbour development policy.
